sections.h2: What are the choices for selling a house in Stockbridge, Georgia?
sections.html:
A Stockbridge homeowner can hire an agent and list the house, handle the sale personally, or take a direct offer from a cash buyer. The listing route usually brings the widest pool of buyers. A direct sale gives up some of that price pressure in return for speed and fewer conditions.

  • List with an agent when the house is in good shape and you can allow time for a buyer's loan and appraisal.
  • Sell without an agent if you are comfortable pricing the house, screening buyers and managing the contract.
  • Choose a cash sale when repairs, back taxes, a tenant or an estate make a conventional listing hard.

Whichever way you go, Henry County property tax and the state transfer tax apply, and both are covered below with the offices that handle them.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Stockbridge homes and households?
sections.html:
Stockbridge is mostly a city of owners: the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates put the owner-occupied rate at 56.0 percent, with 14,320 households. The population estimate for July 1, 2025 is 36,331, compared with 28,973 in the 2020 census and 25,636 in 2010.

About 80.7 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, a sign of a settled owner base. The mean commute is 31.0 minutes, and the plan ties the city's growth to commuting along I-75.

sections.h2: How did Stockbridge develop along the railroad and I-75?
sections.html:
The city's comprehensive plan update traces the modern town to a railroad depot built about a mile south of an older settlement, after two Atlanta businessmen bought land and offered it at a reasonable price. Stockbridge incorporated as a town in 1895 and as a city on August 6, 1920. The depot, which stood roughly 600 feet north of North Henry Boulevard, was torn down by the Southern Railway in the early 1980s.

Growth followed the interstate. The plan says much of the city's development came with highway construction that began in the area in the late 1960s, once commuting to and from Atlanta got easier. Today the city sits close to I-75, I-675 and Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport. That location is the first thing most buyers ask about, so it belongs in any listing description or cash offer conversation.

sections.h2: Which roads and services matter to Stockbridge buyers?
sections.html:
Buyers weigh the drive to I-75 first. The city plan names a Georgia Regional Transportation Authority park and ride on the north side of I-75 at State Route 138, and another near Mount Zion Parkway south of the interstate. It reports that the two Xpress bus routes leaving Stockbridge rank among the top three for ridership across the whole system.

  • Rock Quarry Road is slated for widening from two lanes to four over 2.6 miles between Eagles Landing Parkway and SR 138, which is also US 23 and North Henry Boulevard. The Atlanta Regional Commission approved the funding in July 2018 to ease congestion near Piedmont Henry Hospital.
  • The Henry County Fire Department's Station 9 on Rock Quarry Road answers fire and medical calls in the city, while the Stockbridge Police Department handles law enforcement.
  • Public schools are run by Henry County Schools, and the Cochran Public Library sits on Burke Street.

The plan also lists the Rum Creek Greenway among local amenities and flags downtown revitalization as a continuing goal, with the old rail line described as an obstacle to downtown development.

sections.h2: How does Henry County property tax work for a Stockbridge seller?
sections.html:
Henry County's tax commissioner mails bills to whoever owned the property on January 1, and the bills are due on or before November 16. Interest accrues monthly after the due date, and a 5 percent penalty is added every 120 days, up to a maximum of 20 percent. Payments mailed in must carry a USPS postmark, and metered mail is refused.

If you sold during the year, the county's rule is specific. A tax lien is filed against the January 1 owner unless a settlement statement showing that county taxes were collected reaches the tax commissioner within 90 days of the due date, under Georgia Code 48-3-3. Send the first page of the settlement statement, with the parcel address, to the county's property tax email address listed on its site.

Two other items on a Stockbridge bill can surprise sellers. Streetlight, stormwater and sanitation fees are charged on the same bill, and a county water charge covers the infrastructure whether or not you have a well. Call the departments printed on the bill if a fee looks wrong.

sections.h2: What homestead and appeal deadlines apply in Henry County?
sections.html:
Henry County asks owners to apply for homestead by April 1, in person at either county tax office or online. The Stockbridge office is on Burke Street and the main office is on Henry Parkway in McDonough. The county's FAQ lists the documents: a driver's license showing the property address, vehicle registrations at that address, the warranty deed, and a divorce decree if one applies.

  • A married couple may claim homestead on only one residence.
  • An owner who turns 62 by January 1 can apply for an added school tax reduction, and it steps up at ages 65, 68 and 70.
  • Henry is among the counties the Georgia Department of Revenue lists as having a valuation freeze exemption for homesteads.
  • An assessment appeal must be postmarked within 45 days of the notice of assessment.

Anyone who is behind on taxes should know that Henry County holds judicial in rem tax sales on the first Tuesday of each month at 10:00 AM at 140 Henry Parkway in McDonough.

sections.h2: What transfer steps does a Stockbridge closing involve?
sections.html:
Georgia charges a real estate transfer tax before a deed can be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court. The state's published rate is $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part, plus 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part, and the seller is liable unless the contract says the buyer pays. The online PT-61 form that reports the transfer is filed through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority.

A closing attorney or title company normally handles that filing, the payoff of any mortgage and the recording of the deed. Ask whichever office you pick for a written payoff figure and a draft settlement statement several days before closing so that nothing about the county taxes is left to chance.

sections.h2: What should a Stockbridge seller do first?
sections.html:
1. Find the deed and the Henry County parcel number, and look at the latest assessment notice and tax bill.
  2. Ask the Henry County tax commissioner whether city tax is billed separately or on the same bill as county tax.
  3. Request a payoff statement from the mortgage servicer, and a lien search through the closing attorney.
  4. Collect two or three offers, including a direct cash price, and read each one for repair credits, closing dates and who pays the transfer tax.
  5. Send the settlement statement to the county within 90 days of the tax due date.

faqs.a: Yes. County property tax comes from the Henry County Tax Commissioner, which keeps an office on Burke Street in Stockbridge, and Henry County Schools run the public schools.

faqs.q: When are Henry County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are due on or before November 16 and go to the person who owned the property on January 1. Late balances collect monthly interest and a 5 percent penalty every 120 days, capped at 20 percent.

faqs.q: What happens to the tax bill if I sell my Stockbridge house mid-year?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner still receives the bill. Unless a settlement statement showing the county taxes were collected reaches the tax commissioner within 90 days of the due date, a lien is filed against that owner.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay a transfer tax to sell in Stockbridge?
faqs.a: Yes. Georgia requires the real estate transfer tax before a deed is recorded, and the seller is liable by default. The rate is $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Stockbridge that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers purchase as-is, and the repair cost shows up in their price. Get at least two offers and compare them against the cost of repairing the house yourself and waiting for a conventional buyer.
